props.title: Ask the Neighbors

B01.capture_spec: C01-hook: scene spec evidence/planning-checks/scenes/C01-hook.json, 11.6 s clip (stretched to the measured audio), 30 fps, 1280x720 canvas rendered at 3840x2160, Forward+, nearest filter. The same sprite; the outline shader (08-loop, thickness 3) switches on as the voice says 'outline'. Verified: no outline pixels before the switch, a 12 px (3 image px x 4) line after it (planning check C01)
B01.visual_intent: Act title 'Ask the Neighbors' (serif 40) top-left. A real Godot render in a framed window on the cream stage: the teal test sprite sits plain, then the outline shader switches on and a clean indigo line appears around its whole shape. Labels under the sprite: 'shader off', then 'shader on'.
B01.motion_claim: The sprite is plain, then a line appears around it the moment the shader switches on.

show.event: the outline switches on; label 'shader on'

B01.runner_up: manim drawing of a sprite gaining a line
B01.why: A real render is the honest picture of 'an outline switches on'; a drawing would only claim it.

props.videoLabel: Godot 4.7.2 · Forward+ · a plus sign with a tinted copy behind it, scaled 6x to 7.2x

B02.capture_spec: C02-bigcopy: scene spec evidence/planning-checks/scenes/C02-bigcopy.json, 13.9 s clip (stretched to the measured audio), 30 fps, 1280x720 canvas rendered at 3840x2160, Forward+, nearest filter. A plus-shaped sprite (drawn 6x) with a tinted copy behind it that grows by a fifth (6x to 7.2x): tips thick, sides thin. Verified: tip border 10 px, side border 3 px, ratio about 3 (analyze_bigcopy H1); the scene frame at 6x to 7.2x reads 29 and 9 px (analyze_scenes C02)
B02.visual_intent: A plus-shaped teal sprite on the stage with a tinted (indigo) copy behind it that grows by a fifth as the voice says it. The copy shows as a thick border at the four tips and a thin one along the sides. Labels 'tip: thick' and 'side: thin' with one ring on each.
B02.motion_claim: The copy swells out from behind the sprite: the border is fat at the tips and thin along the sides.
B02.runner_up: manim drawing with measured tick marks
B02.why: A real render of the actual trick, with the thickness measured (10 px at a tip against 3 px at a side), is more convincing than a drawing.

B03.visual_intent: A pixel grid (outline-only cells, no fill behind text) with the teal test sprite's silhouette as filled cells in the middle. One empty cell beside the sprite gets a terracotta ring and four short arrows to its four neighbors; the right neighbor is a filled cell and lights up. The ringed cell takes the line color (indigo) and a label reads 'on the outline'. Then a cell inside the sprite is asked: its own cell is opaque, label 'keeps its color', and it stays teal.
B03.motion_claim: A ring visits one empty cell, four arrows reach out, the right neighbor lights, the cell turns the line color; then a sprite cell is asked and keeps its color.

show.event: grid appears; a small program mark runs over every cell at once
one empty cell ringed, four arrows
the cell takes the line color

B03.why: The question is the concept: a grid of cells with one cell asking is the shape of the idea before any code appears.

B04.visual_intent: The series' uv_square: a square with a 0 to 1 axis across the top and down the left side (the second axis pointing DOWN). A terracotta dot rests at the middle with the glossary line 'UV: a point's address on the shape, 0 to 1 across, 0 to 1 down'. A second dot hops one small step to the right with a short arrow and the label 'UV + step'. A one-line code label 'texture(TEXTURE, UV + step)' types in under the square, with the glossary line 'TEXTURE: the node's own picture; texture(TEXTURE, uv) reads it' beside it.
B04.motion_claim: The address dot hops one small step to the right, and the code line names exactly that hop.

show.event: square with axes, address dot at the middle
the dot hops right; code line types in

B04.why: An address that hops one step is a motion; the code line is the label, not the picture.

B05.visual_intent: One pixel's color drawn as four outline boxes in a row: r, g, b, a (monospace labels). The fourth box lifts out and drops onto a 0 to 1 scale with two marks: 0 'empty' (a swatch showing stage color through) and 1 'opaque' (a solid teal swatch). The code fragment '.a' is drawn beside the lifted box.
B05.motion_claim: The fourth box lifts out of the row and lands on a 0 to 1 scale, once at 0 and once at 1.

show.event: four boxes r g b a

B05.runner_up: ClaudeCodeBeat with the line of code
B05.why: Four numbers with the last one lifted out is the picture of '.a'.

B06.visual_intent: The series' ramp strip as a color strip: the sprite's teal at the left end, the line indigo at the right end, end labels 0 and 1 and the glossary line 'mix(a, b, t): blends from a to b: t of 0 gives a, 1 gives b' above. A terracotta marker rides it to 0, then 0.5 (a blend), then 1. Then it continues past the right end to 2 and a small label 'overshoot' appears where the strip has ended.
B06.motion_claim: A marker rides a color strip from teal to indigo and then keeps going past the end of the strip.
B06.why: A marker riding a strip is mix; overshoot is the marker leaving the strip.

cues.label: mix: blends from a to b by t

B07.capture_spec: C07-paints-the-sprite: scene spec evidence/planning-checks/scenes/C07-paints-the-sprite.json, 13.6 s clip (stretched to the measured audio), 30 fps, 1280x720 canvas rendered at 3840x2160, Forward+, nearest filter. The plain sprite; the first try (02-paints-the-sprite) switches on as the voice says 'look what happens': almost the whole sprite turns line colour. Verified: no outline pixels before the switch, then 95.8 percent of the sprite's pixels (71,112 of 74,192 at x4; 4,406 of 4,637 = 95.0 percent at 1:1) come out line coloured (analyze_scenes C07; analyze_lab A10)
B07.visual_intent: Code card at left (the nine-line shader); at right a real Godot window: the plain sprite, then, as the voice says 'look what happens', the first try switches on and the whole sprite turns indigo except a thin teal crescent on its right edge.
B07.motion_claim: The around line is highlighted, then the COLOR line; then the plain sprite turns blue the moment the shader switches on.

show.event: the shader switches on, the sprite turns blue; readout 'all said yes'

B07.why: The bug appearing: a plain sprite turns blue the moment the shader switches on, beside the code that did it.

props.videoLabel: Godot 4.7.2 · Forward+ · the shader on the left

B08.capture_spec: C08-one-question: scene spec evidence/planning-checks/scenes/C08-one-question.json, 13.3 s clip (stretched to the measured audio), 30 fps, 1280x720 canvas rendered at 3840x2160, Forward+, nearest filter. The blue sprite of the first try; as the voice says 'multiply by one minus my own alpha' the fix (03-one-question) switches on: the blue drains off, a line on the left only. Verified: before the fix 71,112 of 74,192 sprite px are line coloured; after it 3,080 outline px (x4), all left of the sprite's centre, none on the right, none on the sprite (analyze_scenes C08; 231 at 1:1, analyze_lab A2)
B08.visual_intent: The same code card with the COLOR line highlighted and '* (1.0 - color.a)' marked; at right a real Godot window: the blue sprite of the first try, then, as the voice says 'multiply by one minus my own alpha', the fix switches on, the blue drains off and the sprite keeps its teal with only a thin indigo line along its left edge. One ring on the line, readout 'left side only'.
B08.motion_claim: The multiplication is highlighted and the blue fill drains off the sprite, leaving a line on its left edge.

show.event: the COLOR line highlighted; the fix switches on and the blue drains off

B08.why: The fix acting: the blue visibly drains off the sprite as the one changed line is highlighted.

B09.capture_spec: C09-lighter-diagonals: scene spec evidence/planning-checks/scenes/C09-lighter-diagonals.json, 11.6 s clip (stretched to the measured audio), 30 fps, 1280x720 canvas rendered at 3840x2160, Forward+, nearest filter. The one-sided line; as the voice says 'all four sides' the four reads (04-lighter-diagonals) switch on: a ring with lighter stretches on the diagonals. Verified: the one-sided line (3,080 px, all left of the centre) becomes a ring of 8,992 px of which 3,328 (37.0 percent) are (128,128,255) (analyze_scenes C09); at 1:1 252 of 672 (37.5 percent), the line colour doubled and clamped, on the diagonal stretches (analyze_lab A3, A11, A14)
B09.visual_intent: Code card (the four reads added into one number, no cap); at right a real Godot window: the one-sided line of the last beat, then, as the voice says 'all four sides', a ring appears around the sprite, its diagonal stretches visibly lighter (periwinkle) than the rest. Two rings on the lighter stretches, readout 'sum = 2'.
B09.motion_claim: The four sides switch on and a ring appears; the sum lines are highlighted, rings land on the lighter diagonal stretches, then the COLOR line.

show.event: the one-sided line becomes a ring

B09.why: The real wrong color, with the code that causes it; the ramp-strip explanation already came one beat earlier.

cues.label: min(a, b): the smaller of two values

B10.capture_spec: C10-four-questions: scene spec evidence/planning-checks/scenes/C10-four-questions.json, 13.6 s clip (stretched to the measured audio), 30 fps, 1280x720 canvas rendered at 3840x2160, Forward+, nearest filter. The ring with lighter stretches; as the voice says 'so mix never overshoots' the cap (05-four-questions) switches on: a uniform ring. Verified: before the cap 3,328 of 8,992 ring px are the wrong colour, after it 0 (analyze_scenes C10; analyze_lab A3)
B10.visual_intent: The same code card with min(around, 1.0) marked; at right a real Godot window: the ring with lighter stretches, which settles, as the voice says 'so mix never overshoots', into a clean ring of one blue all the way round the sprite. Readout 'same blue'.
B10.motion_claim: min(...) is highlighted and the lighter stretches settle to the same blue as the rest.

show.event: the lighter stretches settle to the same blue

B10.why: The fix acting: the light stretches visibly settle to the same blue as the cap is named.
